title: Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey on Bank Lending Practices (SLOOS), 14:00 ET — the first edition whose response window opens after the April-2027 FOMC
source: EST: derived from federalreserve.gov's published 2027 FOMC calendar (monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200 — the July 2027 meeting is 27-28), applied through the release-date rule audited against 67 SLOOS releases 2010-02-01 -> 2026-08-03 during the never-assessed initial research of sloos-2027-05-03, 2026-09-09: the release is the Monday five sessions after the FOMC's final day, shifted to the next business day only when that Monday is a federal holiday or the market is shut (3 exceptions in 67 — 2012-10-31 for Hurricane Sandy, 2018-11-13 and 2024-11-12 for Veterans Day). Wednesday 2027-07-28 + 5 days = Monday 2027-08-02, which is not a federal holiday. Filed estimate because federalreserve.gov publishes no 2027 newsevents page yet (checked 2026-09-09, HTTP 404), because the FOMC calendar carries the Fed's own 'tentative until confirmed at the meeting immediately preceding it' caveat, and because this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep
notes: PROPOSED as the follow-on to sloos-2027-05-03 and the edition that actually answers what May's cannot. The collection arithmetic, derived from 32 editions' published sent/due dates (April editions go out the Monday after the March FOMC, responses due 28-31 days before release): the May-2027 edition's window closes about 2027-04-02, i.e. BEFORE the 2027-04-28 FOMC — so the July-2027 survey, sent about 2027-06-21 and due about 2027-07-01, is the first structured read on how the April AND June decisions transmit into bank credit standards. That makes this the score-by edition for anything the May one leaves open. Corridor is far cleaner than May's: 2027-08-02 is a Monday and the first trading day of August, but it does not sit on a Treasury borrowing-estimates release (Treasury's own refunding-week Monday for August 2027 is the Monday before the refunding Wednesday, which the treasury lane owns and this one does not derive). Impact low for the measured reason carried by every SLOOS entry on this calendar: KRE's close-to-close excess vs SPY across 67 modern-regime releases is +0.109%, permutation p=0.496, and only two releases exceed KRE's own p90, both with named non-SLOOS causes. Estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
